Author: Anil Kumar Choudhary
Bench: Anil Kumar Choudhary

In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi

3. The learned senior counsel for the petitioner files the supplementary affidavit dated 12.08.2024.
Keep the same in the record.

4. This Criminal Miscellaneous Petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure with a prayer to quash the criminal prosecution against the petitioner in Complaint Case No. 1699 of 2016 of the Court of Judicial Magistrate -1st Class, Ranchi including the order taking cognizance dated 05.08.2017 whereby cognizance has been taken for the offences punishable under Section 420, 467, 468 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code.

5. The allegation against the petitioner is that the co- accused -Prem Bhaskar has prepared a registered power of attorney purportedly executed in his favour by the complainant and by virtue of the said power of attorney, the co-accused -Prem Dharmendra Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27426113/

6. It is submitted by the learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner, relying upon the Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Randheer Singh Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others, reported in (2021) 14 SCC 626, para -33 of which reads as under:-
"33.

entities.text: Randheer Singh Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others, reported in (2021) 14 SCC 626
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, it appears that criminal proceedings are being taken recourse to as a weapon of harassment against a purchaser.
It is reiterated at the cost of repetition that the FIR does not disclose any offence so far as the appellant is concerned.
There is no whisper of how and in what manner, this appellant is involved in any criminal offence and the charge- sheet, the relevant part whereof has been extracted above, is absolutely vague.
There can be no doubt that jurisdiction under Section 482CrPC should be used sparingly for the purpose of preventing abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice.

Whether a complaint discloses criminal offence or not depends on the nature of the allegation and whether the essential ingredients of a criminal offence are present or not has to be judged by the High Court.
There can be no doubt that a complaint disclosing civil transactions may also have a criminal texture.
The High Court has, however, to see whether the dispute of a civil nature has been given colour of criminal offence.

In such a situation, the High Court should not hesitate to quash the criminal proceedings as held by this Court in Paramjeet Batra [ Batra v. State of Uttarakhand, (2013) 11 SCC 673 : (2012)
4 SCC (Cri) 76] extracted above."
That this criminal proceeding has been taken recourse to, as a weapon for harassment, against the bonafide purchaser of a land.

sentences.text: 7. It is next submitted by the learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner that there is no allegation that the petitioner has any role in the alleged forging of the power of attorney claimed to be a forged one purportedly executed by the complainant in favour of the co-accused - Prem Bhaskar.
It is then submitted that there is no allegation against the petitioner of inducing the complainant in any manner to deliver any property etc..

It is next submitted by the learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner, drawing attention of this Court to annexure-6 of the supplementary affidavit dated 12.08.2024 that the same Flat has already been sold by the complainant along with one Santosh Kumar Singh to Mrs. Sudha Singh on 26.05.2012 and this material fact has been suppressed in the complaint which was filed on 28.06.2016 much after the same.

It is next submitted that though the petitioner has paid full price of the Flat involved in this case but the petitioner himself has left the Flat in the month of November, 2015 and it is in the occupation of the complainant.
Hence, it is submitted that the prayer as prayed for in this criminal miscellaneous petition be allowed.

8. Learned Addl. P.P. appearing for the State vehemently opposes the prayer made by the petitioner in this criminal miscellaneous petition and submits that the allegations made in this criminal miscellaneous petition if considered to be true in their entirety, the offences alleged against the Dharmendra Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27426113/
2 petitioner is made out.

entities.text: Dharmendra Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is lastly submitted that this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit be dismissed.

9. Having heard the rival submissions made at the Bar and after carefully going through the materials available in the record, this Court finds that the main allegation of forging the power of attorney executed by the complainant is against Prem Bhaskar.
There is no allegation against the petitioner of having any role played in the same nor is there any allegation against the petitioner of cheating the complainant in any manner.

Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that even if the entire allegations against the petitioner are considered to be true, still the offence for which the learned Judicial Magistrate found prima-facie case against the petitioner is not made out.
Hence, this Court is of the considered view that the continuation of this criminal proceeding against the petitioner will amount to abuse of process of law.

Therefore, this is a fit case where the criminal prosecution against the petitioner in Complaint Case No. 1699 of 2016 of the Court of Judicial Magistrate -1st Class, Ranchi including the order dated 05.08.2017 whereby the learned Judicial Magistrate-1st Class, Ranchi has found prima facie case for the offences punishable under Section 420, 467, 468 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code be quashed and set aside qua the petitioner.
10.

Accordingly, the criminal prosecution against the petitioner in Complaint Case No. 1699 of 2016 of the Court of Judicial Magistrate -1st Class, Ranchi including the order dated 05.08.2017 whereby the learned Judicial Magistrate-1st Class, Ranchi has found prima facie case for the offences punishable under Section 420, 467, 468 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code is quashed and set aside qua the petitioner only.
11.
This criminal miscellaneous petition is disposed of accordingly.

(Anil Kumar Choudhary, J.) High Court of Jharkhand, Ranchi Dated, the 13th August, 2024 AFR/Sonu-Gunjan/-
